sections.h2: Alamance County tax office and housing snapshot
sections.html:
One county department lists, values and collects tax on everything taxable. It sits at 124 W. Elm St. in Graham, opens weekdays from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., and answers at (336) 228-1312. Graham is the county seat and Burlington is the largest community, with Elon, Haw River, Green Level, Ossipee, Swepsonville and Alamance inside the county lines and parts of Mebane and Gibsonville as well.

The 2020 count was 171,415 residents, and the July 2025 estimate of 186,177 is 8.6% higher. Median home value for 2020 to 2024 was $241,500, owners live in 65.0% of homes, and builders took out 2,027 permits in 2025. Check your own parcel in the county property record search before you name a price.

Four things shape a sale here: the January 1 listing date, the September 1 due date, the 2027 revaluation, and a delinquent tax check at recording.

The tax year is fixed on January 1: whoever owns a parcel that day is the person billed. Statements arrive in July, and a payment made by January 5 owes no interest.

Alamance County tax calendar and relief deadlines
DateWhat happens
January 1Listing date; owner on this day is billed
January 1 to 31Filing window for present-use and exemption applications
June 1Deadline for elderly, disabled, circuit breaker and disabled veteran relief
JulyBills mailed
September 1Bills due
January 5Last day to pay with no interest
January 6Delinquent; 2% interest added, then 0.75% on the sixth of each later month

A house bought after January 1 can still produce a bill in the seller's name, even after the deed is recorded and the record is updated. Correct the mailing address ahead of July so the bill finds you.

You can pay by mail (the postmark counts), in an indoor or outdoor drop box (credited as of the drop date), or online with a convenience fee. Registered vehicles are billed separately by the state through Tag and Tax Together when you renew your registration.

Every parcel in Alamance County is being revalued effective January 1, 2027, and notices of value are scheduled to be mailed February 15, 2027. The last revaluation took effect January 1, 2023. North Carolina requires reappraisal at least every eight years under G.S. 105-286, and Alamance chose to do it every four.

Vincent Valuations, which helped with the 2023 work, is doing the 2027 appraisal. Staff spend roughly two years in the field checking property features, comparing sales and noting improvements. The target is to land at or close to 100% of market value.

Seeing a bigger value on the notice does not guarantee a bigger bill, since rates tend to fall as values rise, and a revenue neutral rate would keep the typical owner near last year's payment. A parcel that gained more than average pays more, and one that lagged pays less.

Planning to sell in 2027? Open the notice the day it arrives. Your appeal period runs from its date, and late filings are generally turned away. For revaluation questions, call the same number as the tax department, (336) 228-1312.

sections.h2: How to appeal your property value
sections.html:
Start with an informal review by county appraisers. If that leaves a dispute, the Board of Equalization and Review hears it. The filing window depends on the kind of property.

  • Real property: during the annual listing period, with documentation such as sales, photos, repair estimates or an appraisal.
  • Business and individual personal property: thirty days from the notice of value.
  • Registered vehicles: thirty days after the due date shown on the combined tag and tax notice.

The local board starts deliberating about the first week of April and gives each side a fixed amount of time. Losing at the local level opens the door to the Property Tax Commission in Raleigh. It works like a trial, applies evidence rules and places the burden on the taxpayer.

Common grounds include a value above the likely sale price, wrong square footage or condition on the record, and nearby sales that point lower. A comparable sales tool and a property record search are on the county site to help you gather proof.

June 1 is the usual filing deadline, and income caps change yearly, so ask the tax department for current figures. An online eligibility calculator on the county site covers four of the programs.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: shelters the larger of $25,000 or half the home's taxable value, subject to an income cap.
  • Circuit breaker deferral: postpones part of the tax on a permanent residence, scaled to income. Owners must be 65 or older, or disabled, with five years of ownership and residence behind them.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: shelters the first $45,000 of assessed value for an honorably discharged veteran with a total, permanent service-connected disability, or for a surviving spouse. Age and income do not matter.
  • Present-use value: taxes qualifying farm, horticulture and forestry land on its use, but taxes deferred for the previous three years can be recaptured if the land leaves the program.

Selling while a deferral or present-use status is in place? Ask about payoff or recapture amounts before you agree to a closing date.

sections.h2: What the county checks when a deed is recorded
sections.html:
Since May 2, 2011, each deed to be recorded, except timber deeds and releases, goes to the county Tax Department first for delinquent tax certification (G.S. 161-31(b)). A seller with back taxes should clear them so the certification can be issued.

After recording, the change reaches the property record in a short chain. The Register of Deeds keeps the document and assigns it a book and page number. Land Records staff review it, update the owner name and mailing address, and send the change to the online record and GIS map. A simple sale of an existing parcel moves faster than a split or a new subdivision. If nothing shows up after several weeks, call Land Records with the book and page number.

When an owner has died, the county follows the estate file at the Clerk of Superior Court or recorded documents. Bills stay due on schedule meanwhile, and staff ask for the estate file number, the parcel number or address, and a mailing address.

Sort the tax side out before you set a closing date. Find out who is billed for the current year, since the January 1 owner gets the bill. Ask the tax department whether any back taxes would stop the deed from being certified. If a deferral or present-use status applies, get the payoff or recapture figure in writing. Then split the year's cost with the buyer at closing and check that the mailing address on the record is correct. A cash sale does not remove any of these steps, but it can shorten the wait around them.

faqs.q: When are Alamance County property taxes due?
faqs.a: September 1. Interest starts January 6, so a bill paid by January 5 carries none. After that, 2% is added, plus 0.75% on the sixth of each following month.

faqs.q: Whose name is on the bill after an early-year purchase?
faqs.a: A bill can still arrive under the prior owner's name, because the county lists parcels to the January 1 owner. Divide the cost at closing and fix the mailing address before July.

faqs.q: When will new values from the 2027 revaluation arrive?
faqs.a: Notices of value are scheduled to be mailed February 15, 2027, for the January 1, 2027 effective date. Your appeal deadline is tied to the date on that notice.

faqs.q: What is the deadline for tax relief programs in Alamance County?
faqs.a: June 1 for the elderly or disabled exclusion, the circuit breaker deferral and the disabled veteran exclusion. Present-use and exemption filings fall in the January listing window.

faqs.q: Who do I call at Alamance County Tax Administration?
faqs.a: Call (336) 228-1312 or visit 124 W. Elm St. in Graham, weekdays from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. The same number handles revaluation questions.
